ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r4.claim: God tolerates arrogance and disorder only while expedient, then destroys those whose collective existence threatens the world; Thamūd exemplify the warning to Quraysh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r4.anchor: When these things cross the bounds, the Almighty destroys them and cleanses His world from people whose existence becomes dangerous for it in their collective capacity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p330/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p330/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p330/r1.claim: The Quraysh are warned that if they adopt Thamūd’s arrogant attitude, God will seize them and no one can help.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p330/r1.anchor: no one would be able to help them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r4.claim: Nations are punished collectively in this world for collective rebellion, while each person is individually judged and rewarded or punished in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r4.anchor: In the Hereafter, each person will be held accountable in his personal capacity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r5.claim: Historical evidence shows that a rebellious nation is given time and a clear warning, then destroyed if it persists in denial without excuse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r5.anchor: it is communicated the truth to the extent that it is left with no excuse to deny the truth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r1.claim: Cosmic and inward evidence mainly serves reflective intellectuals; historical incidents can move ordinary people who are able to learn from them, so the Qur’an uses both forms of proof.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r1.anchor: evidence from incidents and events are more effective

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r2.claim: The Qur’an mentions Thamūd alone here, although it names many nations elsewhere; its history was especially familiar to the Quraysh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r2.anchor: has mentioned many nations to highlight this aspect

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r3.claim: Islahi quotes his mentor Imām Farāhī: Quraysh knew the Thamūd’s history, and the Qur’anic allusion was enough to evoke the whole account, including their inherited settlements and traditions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r3.anchor: has discussed their history and their resemblance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r4.claim: The brief Qur’anic account could evoke the Thamūd’s full fate for the Quraysh because their history was familiar and often discussed among them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r4.anchor: was enough to point to their complete history

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r5.claim: A cited Arabic couplet treats Qidār as a figure overcome by time, evidence that Thamūd were known in Arab poetry.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p338/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p338/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p338/r1.claim: Qidār, who killed the she-camel, was an autocratic and rebellious Thamūd leader, comparable to Qayl ibn ʿUmar of ʿĀd.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p338/r1.anchor: He was an autocratic and rebellious leader

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p338/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p338/r2.speaker: al-Afwah al-Awdī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p338/r2.claim: Al-Afwah compares his nation’s corrupt elements to Qayl and Qidār, portraying them as destructive, resistant to guidance, and driven by folly and rebellion.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r1.claim: Thamūd’s rebellion, leaders’ deviance, and fate were proverbial among Arabs, so the Qur’an’s short reference conveyed a full history to its first audience.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r1.anchor: so well known to the Arabs

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r4.claim: Qidār’s callousness led the nation toward destruction; the verb describing his rising means preparing for the crime that opened God’s wrath.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r4.anchor: which opened the doors of God’s wrath on the whole nation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r5.claim: After Ṣāliḥ warned them, Thamūd demanded a sign; he made the she-camel both a sign of punishment and a test with an assigned drinking turn.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r5.anchor: nominated a she-camel as a sign for this punishment

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r6.claim: After Thamūd hamstrung the camel, God gave them three days to repent; the respite increased their arrogance, and punishment destroyed them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r7.claim: Ṣāliḥ’s words describe his final warning to Thamūd to honor God’s she-camel and her turn to drink or face punishment.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r1.claim: The accusative phrase about God’s she-camel uses tahdhīr, with an omitted warning verb that focuses the listener; the warning style is common across languages.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r1.anchor: in the accusative on account of

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r13.claim: If Ashqāhā is collective, the pronoun in لهم most naturally refers to it; otherwise it may refer to Thamūd. The messenger is Ṣāliḥ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r13.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في لهم عائد على أقرب مذكور وهو أشقاها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r14.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r14.claim: The majority read nāqata Allāh in the accusative as a warning with an omitted verb, like a repeated warning; do not harm God's she-camel or withhold its water.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r14.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ناقة الله بنصب التاء، وهو منصوب على التحذير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r1.claim: The majority say Thamūd were unbelievers; a report says they had followed Ṣāliḥ for a time, then disbelieved and hamstrung the camel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r1.anchor: وروي أنهم كانوا قد أسلموا قبل ذلك وتابعوا صالحا بمدة، ثم كذبوا وعقروا

BURSEVI:v10p345/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p345/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p345/r2.claim: The Messenger is Salih ibn Ubayd ibn Jabir ibn Thamud ibn Aws ibn Iram; calling him Messenger signals the duty to obey and the depth of their defiance.
BURSEVI:v10p345/r2.anchor: وهو صالح عليه السلام ابن عبيد بن جابر بن ثمود بن عوص بن أرم فالإضافة للعهد

BURSEVI:v10p345/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p345/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p345/r3.claim: Naqat Allah is an accusative warning formula; the camel belongs to God honorifically and proves His unity, power, and Salih's prophethood, so they must not harm it.
BURSEVI:v10p345/r3.anchor: منصوب على التحذير وإن لم يكن من الصور التي يجب فيها حذف العامل

BURSEVI:v10p345/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p345/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p345/r4.claim: The camel had an assigned share of water on one day while Thamud and their livestock drank on another, which they resented.
BURSEVI:v10p345/r4.anchor: فإنها كان لها شرب يوم معلوم ولهم ولمواشيهم شرب يوم آخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r7.claim: The first fa sequences the denial and Salih's challenge: he showed the she-camel as a sign and warned them not to harm it or deprive it of its turn to drink.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r7.anchor: فتحداهم بآية الناقة وحذرهم من التعرض لها بسوء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r8.claim: The later 'they denied him' means they rejected the warning and its threatened punishment; thus the she-camel sign followed an earlier rejection, as in the account in Sūrat Hūd.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r8.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أن آية الناقة أرسلت لهم بعد أن كذبوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r1.claim: Alternatively, the fa merely introduces details after a general statement, as in other Quranic examples; Thamūd denied through arrogance when their most wicked man rose, with the warning and hamstringing then elaborating the episode.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الفاء للترتيب الذكري المجرد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r3.claim: Nāqata Allāh is accusative as a warning: beware God's she-camel means do not harm her, with the command attached to the creature but intended for people's conduct.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r4.claim: The possessive honors the she-camel as God's sign confirming Salih's mission and as a miraculous creature.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r4.anchor: وإضافة { ناقة } إلى اسم الجلالة لأنها آية جعلها الله على صدق رسالة صالح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r5.claim: Siqyāhā is a verbal noun following the warning: beware taking her allotted water, with either an omitted noun such as the water source or a source term used for the water itself.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r6.claim: The intended prohibition is inferred from context: they must not water their camels on her day, since the word siqyā points to her assigned turn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r6.anchor: فإن مادة سقيا تؤذن بأن المراد التحذير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r7.claim: The denial following the warning is a second denial: they rejected the threat implied by the prohibition, as stated explicitly in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r7.anchor: والتكذيب المعقب به تحذيره إياهم بقوله : { ناقة الله } ، تكذيب ثانن

AKHFASH:v2p580/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p580/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p580/r2.claim: Nāqat Allāh means God's she-camel, followed by the warning to beware harming her.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p142#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p142#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p142#3/r1.claim: God's messenger here is Ṣāliḥ; the camel is accusative as a warning, since warnings take the accusative, as al-Farrāʾ explains.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p142#3/r1.anchor: وهو صالح ناقة الله قال الفراء نصب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p142#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p142#3/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p142#3/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba paraphrases Ṣāliḥ's warning as “beware God's she-camel and her drinking.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p142#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة المعنى احذروا ناقة الله وشربها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p142#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p142#3/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p142#3/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj paraphrases it as “leave God's she-camel and leave her drinking”; commentators explain that her water-drinking turn was protected.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p142#3/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج المعنى ذروا ناقة الله و ذروا سقياها قال المفسرون سقياها شربها

IBNKATHIR:91:13/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:13/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:91:13/r1.claim: God's messenger here is Salih, who warns Thamud not to harm God's she-camel.
IBNKATHIR:91:13/r1.anchor: وقوله : { فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ } يعني : صالحًا ،   عليه السلام : { نَاقَةُ اللَّهِ } أي : احذروا ناقة الله أن تمسوها بسوء ،

IBNKATHIR:91:13/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:13/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:91:13/r2.claim: Salih also warns them not to violate the she-camel's assigned watering turn: it has one day and the people another known day.
IBNKATHIR:91:13/r2.anchor: { وَسُقْيَاهَا } أي : لا تعتدوا عليها في سقياها ،   فإن لها شرب يوم ولكم شرب يوم معلوم .

FARRA:v3p267/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p267/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p267/r9.claim: Nāqata Allāh is accusative as a warning formula; Arabic warnings normally use the accusative.
FARRA:v3p267/r9.anchor: الله (13) نصبت الناقة على التحذير حذرهم إياها، وكل تحذير فهو نصب

FARRA:v3p267/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p267/r10.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p267/r10.claim: Raising the phrase as “this is God’s she-camel” is also valid and still carries a warning.
FARRA:v3p267/r10.anchor: ولو رفع على ضمير: هذه ناقة الله، فإن العرب قد ترفعه، وفيه معنى التحذير،

FARRA:v3p267/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p267/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p267/r11.claim: Arabic can raise a warning such as “the enemy, the enemy!” or “night, depart”; a poem similarly raises “weapons!” as an urgent command.
FARRA:v3p267/r11.anchor: فاهربوا، وفيه تحذير، وهذا الليل فارتحلوا، فلو قرأ قارئ بالرفع كان مصيبا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530#5/r1.claim: The messenger’s warning means: beware God’s she-camel and her allotted drinking.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530#5/r1.anchor: {فقال لهم رسول الله ناقة الله وسقياها} ؛ أي احذروا ناقة الله (2)

JISHUMI:v10p7434/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r7.claim: Suqyā is one's allotted share of water, as in the verse about the she-camel's and people's shares.
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r7.anchor: والسقيا: الحظ من الماء، وهو النصيب منه، كما قال تعالى:

JISHUMI:v10p7434/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r10.claim: Nāqat Allāh is accusative as an exhortation: tend God's she-camel or beware it, like repeating “the lion.”
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r10.anchor: ناقة الله) نصب على الإغراء؛ أي: عليكم ناقة الله

KASHSHAF:91:13/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:13/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:13/r1.claim: The pronoun them may refer to the most wretched group, since the person who directly killed the camel is most clearly and intensely wretched.
KASHSHAF:91:13/r1.anchor: والضمير في { لَهُمْ } يجوز أن يكون للأشقين والتفضيل في الشقاوة

KASHSHAF:91:13/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:13/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:13/r2.claim: Naqat Allah is an accusative warning, meaning leave the camel alone or beware harming her; do not withhold or monopolize her drinking share.
KASHSHAF:91:13/r2.anchor: و { نَاقَةَ الله } نصب على التحذير ،   كقولك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r6.claim: “God's she-camel” is an accusative warning, with an implied command to leave her alone or beware of harming her.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r6.anchor: و { ناقة الله } نصب على التحذير ، كقولك الأسد الأسد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r7.claim: Her water-share means they must not keep it from her or monopolize it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r7.anchor: { وسقياها } فلا تزووها عنها ، ولا تستأثروا بها عليها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#7/r1.claim: God's Messenger was Salih; the warning “God's she-camel and its drink” is an accusative warning to beware harming her, repeated for emphasis like “the lion, the lion.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#7/r1.anchor: ﴿ فقال لهم رسول الله ﴾ صالح عليه السلام ﴿ ناقة الله ﴾ نصب على التحذير

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r1.anchor: { فقال لهم رسول الله } يعني صالحا

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r2.claim: Naqata is an accusative warning form, meaning beware of harming God’s she-camel.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r2.anchor: { ناقة الله } «ناقة» منصوب على التحذير كقولك: الأسد الأسد

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r3.claim: Alternatively, it means “leave God’s she-camel alone,” as commanded at 7:73.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r3.anchor: وقيل: ذروا ناقة الله، كما قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r4.claim: Suqiyaha means leave her to drink her allotted water, explained earlier at al-Shuara and al-Qamar.

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r5.claim: After the people demanded a camel, it emerged from the rock; her water day alternated with theirs, which troubled them.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r5.anchor: فإنهم لما اقترحوا الناقة، وأخرجها لهم من الصخرة، جعل لهم شرب يوم من بئرهم، ولها شرب يوم مكان ذلك

NAHHAS:v5p237/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p237/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p237/r8.claim: The warning means to beware God's she-camel.

NAHHAS:v5p237/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p237/r9.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p237/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says a reader could use the nominative, with the implied meaning this is God's she-camel.
NAHHAS:v5p237/r9.anchor: قال الفراء ولو قرأ قارىء ناقة الله بالرفع أي هذه ناقة الله لجاز

NAHHAS:v5p237/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p237/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p237/r10.claim: The author rejects inventing a new reading.
NAHHAS:v5p237/r10.anchor: قال أبو جعفر ولا يجوز الابتداع في القراءات

QUTB-ZILAL:91:13/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:13/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:13/r1.claim: Before the attack, Salih warned them not to touch God's she-camel or the water assigned to it.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:13/r1.anchor: احذروا أن تمسوا ناقة الله أو أن تمسوا الماء الذي جعل لها يوما ولهم يوم

QUTB-ZILAL:91:13/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:13/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:13/r2.claim: The camel was made a sign after they requested a miracle; its special nature is left unspecified because God disclosed no details.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:13/r2.anchor: فجعل الله هذه الناقة آية - ولا بد أنه كان لها شأن خاص لا نخوض في تفصيلاته

RAZI-FULL:v31p177#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#2/r1.claim: The messenger is Salih; he warned them that God's she-camel was a sign of divine unity and his prophethood, forbidding harm and interference with her water.
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#2/r1.anchor: المراد من الرسول صالح عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v31p177#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#2/r2.claim: She and their livestock had alternating drinking days, which harmed their herds; Salih had repeatedly warned of punishment, so his brief warning sufficed.
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#2/r2.anchor: كان لها شرب يوم ولهم ولمواشيهم شرب يوم

RAZI-FULL:v31p177#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#2/r3.claim: Nāqat Allāh is an accusative warning construction, elliptically meaning 'leave her alone and beware her watering'; do not withhold it or take it exclusively.

SAMIN-DURR:91:13/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:13/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:91:13/r1.claim: If ashqāhā denotes a group, lahum refers to them; if it denotes one named man, lahum refers to Thamūd.
SAMIN-DURR:91:13/r1.anchor: وإن كان المراد به علما بعينه فالضمير من " لهم " يعود على ثمود.

SAMIN-DURR:91:13/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:13/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:91:13/r2.claim: Nāqat Allāh is an accusative warning, meaning beware God's she-camel; the warning verb must be omitted because the construction is coordinated, one of three contexts requiring omission.
SAMIN-DURR:91:13/r2.anchor: ناقة الله } منصوب على التحذير، أي: احذروا ناقة الله فلا تقربوها، وإضمار الناصب هنا واجب لمكان العطف

SAMIN-DURR:91:13/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:13/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:91:13/r3.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads nāqatu Allāh in the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning this is God's she-camel.
SAMIN-DURR:91:13/r3.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي " ناقة الله " رفعا على خبر ابتداء مضمر، أي: هذه ناقة الله

STUDYQURAN:91:11/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r2.claim: Ṣāliḥ identified the she-camel brought from a rock as God's sign and called the people to justice and God's ordained sharing of water.
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r2.anchor: Ṣāliḥ made it clear to them that a particular she-camel that God had brought forth from a rock was a sign of God

TAB-FULL:v24p449#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p449#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p449#2/r1.claim: The Messenger is Ṣāliḥ, who warned Thamūd to protect God's she-camel and its allotted drinking turn; she had one day and they another.
TAB-FULL:v24p449#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {فقال لهم رسول الله ناقة الله وسقياها} [الشمس: 13] قسم الله الذي قسم لها من هذا الماء

TAB-FULL:v24p449#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p449#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p449#2/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses the camel's watering as God's allotted share of the water.
TAB-FULL:v24p449#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {فقال لهم رسول الله ناقة الله وسقياها} [الشمس: 13] قسم الله الذي قسم لها من هذا الماء

TABATABAI:91:11-15/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r4.claim: The messenger is Ṣāliḥ. “God’s she-camel” and “her drink” are warning constructions: do not harm her or prevent her from taking her assigned turn at the water.
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r4.anchor: المراد برسول الله صالح عليه السلام نبي ثمود، وقوله { ناقة الله } منصوب على التحذير

ZAJJAJ:v5p333/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p333/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p333/r1.claim: Nāqat Allāh is accusative with an implied leave or spare; the she-camel and her watering turn were to be left alone, since she had one day and they another.
ZAJJAJ:v5p333/r1.anchor: (ناقة) منصوب على معنى ذروا ناقة الله، كما قال سبحانه:

TABRISI:91:14/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:91:14/r13.claim: Saqyā is a share or portion of water.
TABRISI:91:14/r13.anchor: والسقيا الحظ من الماء والنصيب منه

TABRISI:91:14/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:91:14/r19.claim: “God's she-camel and its drink” are objects of an implied command: beware the camel and leave its water-share alone.
TABRISI:91:14/r19.anchor: وقوله { ناقة الله وسقياها } منصوب بفعل مضمر أي احذروا ناقة الله

TABRISI:91:14-15/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14-15/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:91:14-15/r1.claim: An unnamed report describes the camel killer as blond, blue-eyed, short, and thick-necked.
TABRISI:91:14-15/r1.anchor: إن عاقر الناقة كان أشقر أزرق قصيرا ملتزق الحلق

TABRISI:91:14-15/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14-15/r2.speaker: الفراء عن الكلبي ومقاتل
TABRISI:91:14-15/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the warning as an implied command to beware God's she-camel and not slaughter it; every warning takes the accusative.
TABRISI:91:14-15/r2.anchor: قال الفراء: حذرهم إياها وكل تحذير فهو نصب والتقدير احذروا ناقة الله

TABRISI:91:14-15/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14-15/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:91:14-15/r3.claim: Her share can mean her drink of water or the water supplied to her; people must not crowd her out.
TABRISI:91:14-15/r3.anchor: أي وشربها من الماء أو ما يسقيها أي فلا تزاحموها فيه

TABRISI:91:14-15/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14-15/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:91:14-15/r4.claim: Her allotted drinking day is contrasted with the people's, as stated in 26:155.
TABRISI:91:14-15/r4.anchor: لها شرب ولكم شرب يوم معلوم

THALABI:v10p214/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p214/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p214/r6.claim: Calling out “God's she-camel” is a warning and prohibition against slaughtering it, like an emphatic cry of “the lion.”
THALABI:v10p214/r6.anchor:
ناقة الله إغراء وتحذير، أي احذروا عقر ناقة الله، كقولك:
الأسد الأسد

THALABI:v10p214/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p214/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p214/r7.claim: Her drinking allotment is her share of water, which the people must not contest; the verse about each side's allotted drink explains this.
THALABI:v10p214/r7.anchor: وسقياها شربها وسقيها من الماء، فلا تزاحموها فيه، كما قال الله سبحانه: لها شرب ولكم شرب يوم معلوم

THALABI:v10p214/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p214/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p214/r8.claim: They denied Ṣāliḥ and hamstrung the she-camel; God then destroyed them for rejecting His messenger and harming the camel.
THALABI:v10p214/r8.anchor: فكذبوه يعني صالحا (عليه السلام) ، فعقروها يعني الناقة فدمدم دمر عليهم وأهلكهم ربهم بذنبهم بتكذيبهم رسوله

THALABI:v10p214/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p214/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p214/r9.claim: “He made it even” means the punishment covered all of them, leaving no one untouched.
THALABI:v10p214/r9.anchor: فسواها فسوى الدمدمة عليهم جميعا، عمهم بها، فلم يفلت منهم أحد

THALABI:v10p214/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p214/r10.speaker: المروج
THALABI:v10p214/r10.claim: He defines damdama as annihilating destruction.

THALABI:v10p214/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p214/r11.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
THALABI:v10p214/r11.claim: Some linguists instead define damdama as persistence, citing the Arab expression for a fat, full camel.
THALABI:v10p214/r11.anchor: وقال بعض أهل اللغة: الدمدمة: الإدامة. تقول العرب: ناقة مدمومة أي سمينة مملوءة

THALABI:v10p214/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p214/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
THALABI:v10p214/r12.claim: He reads fa-dahdama with hāʾ; the two forms are dialectal equivalents, as in the paired verbs for a changed complexion.
THALABI:v10p214/r12.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن الزبير (فدهدم عليهم) بالهاء، وهما لغتان، كقولك امتقع لونه واهتقع

THALABI:v10p214/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p214/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p214/r13.claim: The Hijazis and Syrians read “fa-lā” with fāʾ, as in their codices; others read “wa-lā,” and ʿuqbāhā means its consequence.
THALABI:v10p214/r13.anchor: قرأ أهل الحجاز والشام فلا بالفاء وكذلك هو في مصاحفهم، الباقون بالواو

THALABI:v10p214/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p214/r14.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p214/r14.claim: He takes the subject of “does not fear its outcome” to be God, who fears no one’s claim against Him for destroying them.
THALABI:v10p214/r14.anchor: فقال الحسن: يعني ولا يخاف الله من أحد تبعة في إهلاكهم

THALABI:v10p214/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p214/r15.speaker: الضحاك والسدي والكلبي
THALABI:v10p214/r15.claim: They refer the phrase to the camel-killer and reorder the syntax: the most wretched arose without fearing the consequences.
THALABI:v10p214/r15.anchor: وقال الضحاك والسدي والكلبي: هو راجع إلى العاقر، وفي الكلام تقديم وتأخير

ASAD-NOTES:91:11#n8/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:91:11#n8/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:91:11#n8/r1.claim: The she-camel account is explained in a note on 7:57; the command to let her drink is tied to 26:155.
ASAD-NOTES:91:11#n8/r1.anchor: For the particular reference to the injunction, "Let her drink", see 26:155

ASAD-NOTES:91:11#n8/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:91:11#n8/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:91:11#n8/r2.claim: The camel legend was already well known in pre-Islamic Arabia.
ASAD-NOTES:91:11#n8/r2.anchor: The formulation of this passage shows that the legend of the she-camel was well known

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r1.claim: The Messenger of God here is Ṣāliḥ.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r2.claim: Nāqata Allāh is accusative through an omitted command, meaning “leave God's she-camel alone,” as in the command in 7:73.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: ناقة الله منصوب على معنى ذروا ناقة الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r3.claim: The accusative expresses a warning; warning constructions take the accusative.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء: حذرهم إياها، وكل تحذير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r4.claim: Suqyāh is coordinated with the she-camel and means her drinking, her water-drinking allotment, or what is given to her to drink.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r4.anchor: وقوله: {وسقياها} عطف على ناقة الله، وهو اسم من السقي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r5.claim: Ṣāliḥ told them to leave God's she-camel unhurt and leave her water allotment alone; they were warned they would be punished, but denied that the punishment would come.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p67/r5.anchor: قال الكلبي (¬4)، ومقاتل (¬5): قال لهم صالح: ذروا ناقة الله، فلا تعقروها

WAHIDI-QT:91:13/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:91:13/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:91:13/r1.claim: The Messenger was Salih; he told Thamud to leave God's she-camel and her allotted drinking day alone.
WAHIDI-QT:91:13/r1.anchor: { فقال لهم رسول الله } صالح { ناقة الله } ذروا ناقة الله { وسقياها } وشربها في يومها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r5.claim: God's messenger is Salih, who told them to leave God's she-camel and let her drink on her allotted day.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r5.anchor: فقال لهم رسول الله } [صالح]. { ناقة الله } ذروا ناقة الله { وسقياها } وشربها في يومها.

ELMALILI:91:11-15/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r2.claim: The camel's appointed alternating drinking day was part of the sign; it was to graze freely, and harming it would bring painful punishment.
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r2.anchor: onun suvarılmasına münâvebe suretiyle bir gün tahsis olunmuş

ELMALILI:91:11-15/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r6.claim: The Messenger is Salih, as Hud says; his accusative warning means to beware God's she-camel, the sign given to the Prophet, and not to touch it or its assigned water.
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r6.anchor: tahzir üzere mansub[^2] olmakla fiili mahzuftur.

ELMALILI:91:11-15/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r7.claim: The omitted command is beware or do not touch God's she-camel and its water allotted for her drinking turn.

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r1.claim: Q 91, 89, and 85 contain three Group II allusions to Thamud, Ad, and Pharaoh; alongside Q 105, they are the earliest narrative Quranic texts and the nucleus of later punishment legends.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Der Abschnitt gehört zu den insgesamt drei Passagen in Gruppe II der frühmekkanischen Suren, in denen Anspielungen auf die Ṯamūd, die ʿĀd und auf Pharao begegnen

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r2.claim: The fullest other early-Makkan Thamud account is later Q 54:23–31; shorter allusions also occur in 89, 69, and 51, while Q 85 and 89 connect the story to Pharaoh and Ad.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Eine relativ ausführliche Darstellung der Ṯamūd-Legende findet sich in frühmekkanischer Zeit nur noch in der sicherlich später als Q 91 anzusetzenden Passage 54:23–31

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r3.claim: Umayya b. Abi al-Salt’s likely authentic poem lacks a divine warner and explicit command; the camel’s foal’s curse triggers destruction, and its named culprit Aḥmar is elsewhere associated with Ad, perhaps showing tribal names or traditions overlapped.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Es fehlt die Figur eines göttlich gesandten Warners, dessen expliziten Anweisungen die Ṯamūd zuwider handeln, und ihre Vernichtung wird durch einen Fluch ausgelöst

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r4.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabia reportedly had a practice of dedicating camels, in keeping with the Quranic camel episode.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r4.anchor: Dass der Koran hier altarabisches Überlieferungsgut aufnimmt, wird auch dadurch nahegelegt, dass eine Weihung von Kamelen auch sonst im vorislamischen Arabien praktiziert worden sein soll

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:13:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:13:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:13:anmerkung/r1.claim: Rasūl corresponds to Greek apostolos and Syriac shlīḥā; it already occurs in Group II with a non-biblical Thamud story, later naming Moses, Muhammad, and an angelic messenger.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:13:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Rasūl entspricht gr. apostolos bzw. syr. šlīḥā. Der Begriff erscheint bereits in Gruppe II der frühmekkanischen Suren

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:13:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:13:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:13:anmerkung/r2.claim: The verb arsala first appears in 105:3 for God sending birds against the people of the elephant; later it names sent punishments and warnings or messengers.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:13:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Das zugehörige Verb ʾarsala ist sogar noch früher bezeugt, nämlich in 105:3

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:13:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:13:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:13:anmerkung/r3.claim: The command literally names God’s she-camel and its watering; later verses state the command more fully, and Islamic works report that consecrated camels were exempt from slaughter and other use.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:13:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Von dem Brauch, innerhalb bestimmter Bezirke geweihte Kamelen von der Schlachtung und jeglicher anderweitigen Nutzung auszunehmen, berichten auch spätere islamische Werke über das alte Arabien

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r1.claim: This is the oldest genuine Quranic punishment legend: it recasts the likely pre-Islamic Thamud story as an example of the choice between good and evil and may mirror the Quranic preacher’s rejection by hearers.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r1.anchor: Die vorliegende Sure funktionalisiert die sicherlich bereits in vorkoranischer Zeit bekannte Ṯamūd-Legende als historisches Exempel für die Konsequenzen der zuvor formulierten Alternative von Gut und Böse

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r2.claim: Compared with Umayya’s poem, the Quran adds a divine messenger and an explicit command to spare the camel; the pre-Islamic offense was cultic disrespect toward a consecrated camel, so the Quran theologically reconfigures the inherited story.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r2.anchor: Das Vergehen der Ṯamūd wird bei Umayya als ein Kultfrevel geschildert, als Mißachtung der Unverletzlichkeit eines geweihten Kamels, nicht als Übertretung eines – durch einen prophetischen Boten überbrachten – göttlichen Verbots.

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r5.claim: The Quran omits Umayya’s aftermath in which a lame servant survives, reports the event, and dies, since that addition does not serve the general lesson.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r5.anchor: Die theologische Zuspitzung der koranischen Version wird überdies daran sichtbar, dass hier das bei Umayya erzählte Nachspiel

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:11/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:11/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:11/r1.claim: The account of Thamud exemplifies a community's wrong choice after humans were given the ability to choose good or evil; its destruction is a warning, as in the accounts in al-A'raf and Hud.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:11/r1.anchor: Semûd kavminin yanlış seçimi ve bu yüzden başlarına gelen büyük felâket

ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#2/r1.claim: Ṣāliḥ addresses either all Thamūd or the worst offenders collectively; calling him God's Messenger signals the duty to obey and the depth of their rebellion.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#2/r1.anchor: فقال لهم أي لثمود أو لأشقانا على ما قيل بناء على أن المراد به جمع ولا يأباه وسقياها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#2/r2.claim: ناقة الله is an accusative warning: beware harming God's she-camel; Alusi surveys disputed syntactic conditions and rejects treating it as a command merely to leave or respect her.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#2/r2.anchor: وهو نصب على التحذير وشرطه ليس المحذر منه أو كونه محذرا بما يعده فقط ليقال هو منصوب بتقدير ذروا أو احذروا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#2/r3.claim: They must also protect her allotted drink, neither preventing it on her turn nor taking it for themselves; the proposal that the conjunction means leaving the camel together with her drink is far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#2/r3.anchor: وسقيها أي واحذروا سقياها فلا تتعرضوا بمنعها عنها في نوبتها ولا تستأثروا بها عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#2/r4.speaker: زيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#2/r4.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads God's she-camel in the nominative, construing the phrase as directing their concern to protect her and her watering turn.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي ناقة الله بالرفع فقيل أي همكم ناقة الله وسقياها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p146/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146/r5.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146/r5.claim: An esoteric mapping reads the sun as the divine essence, its brightness as the Muhammadan reality, the moon as possible-being, day as the manifest world, night as contingent existence veiling the Real, heaven as intellect, earth as body, and the camel and its drink as longing and remembrance or reflection.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146/r5.anchor: وذكر بعض أهل التأويل أن الشمس إشارة إلى ذات واجب الوجود سبحانه وتعالى وضحاها إشارة إلى الحقيقة المحمدية والقمر إشارة إلى ماهية الممكن

ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r1.speaker: بعض آخر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r1.claim: Another esoteric scheme identifies the sun with necessary existence or the divine essence, its brightness with the first determination or its existence, the moon with fixed entities or first determination, day and night with manifestations or beauty and majesty, heaven and earth with subtle and dense worlds, and the camel with the spiritual path or the way of law.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r1.anchor: لعيون حجبتها النقط وضحاها إشارة إلى أول التعينات بأي اسم سميته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440/r3.claim: The Messenger is Salih, who warns them to protect God’s she-camel from being hamstrung.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440/r3.anchor: صالح عليه السلام، {ناقة الله} أي احذروا عقر ناقة الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440/r4.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj construes ‘God’s camel’ as an object of an implied command: leave the she-camel and her allocated drinking turn alone.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: منصوب على معنى: ذروا ناقة الله، {وسقياها} شربها

BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r3.claim: God's messenger warns Thamūd to leave God's camel alone and not prevent its allotted drink.
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r3.anchor: أي ذروا ناقة الله واحذروا عقرها. { وسقيها } وسقيها فلا تذودوها عنها

BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r7.claim: A report says reciting al-Shams is like giving charity over everything illuminated by the sun and moon.
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r7.anchor: من قرأ سورة والشمس فكأنما تصدق بكل شيء طلعت عليه الشمس والقمر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r5.claim: Calling Ṣāliḥ the Messenger of God magnifies both the messenger and the sender; the camel is likewise marked as God's by a divine sign.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r5.anchor: أي الملك الذي له الأمر كله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r6.claim: Nāqat Allāh denotes the divinely honored miracle camel; the implied command is to beware harming her, especially on her water allotment.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r6.anchor: أي الملك الأعظم الذي له الجبروت كله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r7.claim: The command about her drinking means not to drive her from her well on her assigned day or touch her with harm; Ṣāliḥ likely repeated the warning when he sensed their intent.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r7.anchor: أي الماء الذي جعله الله تعالى لها لسقيها

DURR-FULL:v8p530/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r1.claim: The command is to leave God's she-camel and the water portion assigned to her alone.
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r1.anchor: {ناقة الله وسقياها} قال: يقول الله: خلوا بينها وبين قسم الله الذي قسم لها من هذا الماء

TAB:91:13/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:13/r1.speaker: author
TAB:91:13/r1.claim: The Messenger of God is Salih, who warns Thamud to beware God’s she-camel and her allotted watering turn; God had assigned the camel one day and the people another.
TAB:91:13/r1.anchor: يعني بذلك جلّ ثناؤه : صالحا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، فقال لثمود صالح : ناقَةَ اللّهِ وَسُقْياها احذروا ناقة الله وسقياها ، وإنما حذرهم سقيا الناقة

TAB:91:13/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:13/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:91:13/r2.claim: Qatada interprets the camel’s watering as the share of water God apportioned to her.
TAB:91:13/r2.anchor: عن قتادة فَقالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللّهِ ناقَةَ اللّهِ وسُقْياها قَسْم الله الذي قسم لها من هذا الماء

BURHAN:v2p324/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p324/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v2p324/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says every Qur'anic address is followed by religious understanding, through commands, prohibitions, admonitions, warnings, or stories.
BURHAN:v2p324/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري رحمه الله كل نداء في كتاب الله يعقبه فهم في الدين اما من ناحية الاوامر

BURHAN:v2p324/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p324/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p324/r4.claim: The phrase combines warning and exhortation: understand ناقة الله as “beware the she-camel; do not approach her,” with an omitted exhortation to keep to her.
BURHAN:v2p324/r4.anchor: وقد اجتمعا في قوله تعالى ﴿ ناقة الله وسقياها ﴾ 3 والاغراء أمر معناه الترغيب والتحريض

BURHAN:v2p324/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p324/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
BURHAN:v2p324/r8.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ says يا زيد is not a proposition capable of truth or falsehood; it functions like pointing and calling out.
BURHAN:v2p324/r8.anchor: قال أبو البقاء ( 7 ) في شرح الايضاح ذهب الجميع إلى ان قولك يا زيد ليس بخبر محتمل

BURHAN:v2p324/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p324/r9.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
BURHAN:v2p324/r9.claim: Most grammarians do not treat يا فاسق as a proposition, but Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī does because it attributes فسق to the addressee.
BURHAN:v2p324/r9.anchor: واختلفوا في قولك ( 8 ) يافاسق فالاكثرون على انه ليس بخبر ايضا قال أبو علي الفارسي خبر

BURHAN:v3p105/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p105/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p105/r1.claim: One cause of ellipsis is brevity and avoiding redundancy when the situation itself supplies the omitted subject, as in الهلال والله.
BURHAN:v3p105/r1.anchor: فمنها مجرد الاختصار والاحتراز عن العبث بناء على الظاهر نحو الهلال والله

BURHAN:v3p105/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p105/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p105/r2.claim: The verse omits imperatives in a warning and an exhortation: beware the she-camel and do not approach her; keep to what is required of her.
BURHAN:v3p105/r2.anchor: وقد اجتمعا في قوله تعالى ﴿ ناقة الله وسقياها ﴾ 1 على التحذير أي احذروا ناقة الله

BURHAN:v3p105/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p105/r7.speaker: سيبويه
BURHAN:v3p105/r7.claim: Sībawayh gives common reductions as ease-driven omissions: لا أدر for لا أدري, لم أبل for لم أبال, and لم يك for لم يكن.
BURHAN:v3p105/r7.anchor: قال سيبويه العرب تقول لا أدر فيحذفون الياء والوجه لا أدري

ITQAN:v3p222#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p222#2/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p222#2/r5.claim: The vocative form can serve figuratively as both an inducement and a warning; ‘God’s she-camel and its drink’ combines them.
ITQAN:v3p222#2/r5.anchor: وقد ترد صورة النداء لغيره مجازا كالإغراء والتحذير وقد اجتمعا في قوله تعالى ﴿ ناقة الله وسقياها ﴾

ITQAN:v4p394/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p394/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p394/r11.claim: The Messenger of God is Salih.
ITQAN:v4p394/r11.anchor: 5767 ﴿ فقال لهم رسول الله ﴾ هو صالح

ITQAN:v3p153/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p153/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p153/r1.claim: Deletion can achieve brevity and avoid needless repetition; here the warning “God’s she-camel” implies “leave her,” while “her watering” implies “keep to it.”
ITQAN:v3p153/r1.anchor: فناقة الله تحذير بتقدير ( ذروا ) و ( سقياها ) إغراء بتقدير ( الزموا )

ITQAN:v3p153/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p153/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p153/r2.claim: Another purpose of ellipsis is to signal that time is too short to state the omitted material without losing what matters.
ITQAN:v3p153/r2.anchor: ومنها التنبيه على أن الزمان يتقاصر عن الإتيان بالمحذوف وأن الاشتغال بذكره يفضي إلى تفويت المهم

ITQAN:v3p153/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p153/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p153/r3.claim: Ellipsis can magnify and exalt what remains ambiguous.
ITQAN:v3p153/r3.anchor: ومنها التفخيم والإعظام لما فيه من الإبهام

ITQAN:v3p153/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p153/r4.speaker: حازم
ITQAN:v3p153/r4.claim: Hazim says ellipsis is apt when its meaning is strongly indicated or when listing many details would be long and tedious; context lets listeners supply them, especially to provoke wonder or terror.
ITQAN:v3p153/r4.anchor: قال حازم في منهاج البلغاء إنما يحسن الحذف لقوة الدلالة عليه أو يقصد به تعديد أشياء

ITQAN:v3p153/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p153/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p153/r9.claim: A further reason for ellipsis is that only one completion can fit, as in “Knower of the unseen and seen” and “Doer of whatever He wills.”
ITQAN:v3p153/r9.anchor: ومنها كونه لا يصلح إلا له نحو ﴿ عالم الغيب والشهادة ﴾ ﴿ فعال لما يريد ﴾

ABUHAYYAN:91:13/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:13/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:91:13/r1.claim: The pronoun in lahum may refer to al-ashqā if it means a group, or to Thamūd.
ABUHAYYAN:91:13/r1.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في { لهم } عائد على أقرب مذكور وهو { أشقاها } إذا أريد به الجماعة ، ويجوز أن يعود على { ثمود } .

ABUHAYYAN:91:13/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:13/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:91:13/r3.claim: The majority read nāqata Allāhi in the accusative as a warning construction with an elided verb; coordination makes it a repeated warning, “beware the she-camel and her watering.”
ABUHAYYAN:91:13/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { ناقة الله } بنصب التاء ، وهو منصوب على التحذير مما يجب إضمار عامله

ABUHAYYAN:91:13/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:13/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:91:13/r4.claim: Coordination makes the warning construction repeat, as in “the lion, the lion”: beware God’s she-camel and her watering.
ABUHAYYAN:91:13/r4.anchor: لأنه قد عطف عليه ، فصار حكمه بالعطف حكم المكرر ، كقولك : الأسد الأسد

ALUSI:91:13/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:13/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:13/r1.claim: He takes the addressees to be Thamud; a reported alternative takes them as the most wretched one, understood collectively, compatible with the plural watering reference.
ALUSI:91:13/r1.anchor: أي لثمود أو لأشقاها على ما قيل بناءً أن المراد به جمع ولا يأباه وسقياها

ALUSI:91:13/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:13/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:13/r2.claim: The Messenger is Salih; calling him by his office signals that obedience to him is obligatory and highlights their extreme insolence.
ALUSI:91:13/r2.anchor: هو صالح عليه السلام وعبر عنه بعنوان الرسالة إيذاناً بوجوب طاعته

ALUSI:91:13/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:13/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:13/r3.claim: Naqat Allah is accusative as a warning; Makkī explains the conditions for the construction, which need not involve repeating the warning.
ALUSI:91:13/r3.anchor: وهو نصب على التحذير وشرطه ليس تكرير المحذر منه

ALUSI:91:13/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:13/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:13/r4.claim: The warning can be expanded as beware slaughtering God's she-camel, though the omitted complement need not appear in the wording.
ALUSI:91:13/r4.anchor: والكلام على حذف مضاف أي احذروا عقر ناقة الله

ALUSI:91:13/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:13/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:13/r5.claim: The suggested estimate make much of or cling to God's she-camel is rejected as unsound.
ALUSI:91:13/r5.anchor: وجوز أن يكون التقدير عظموا أو الزموا ناقة الله وليس بشيء

ALUSI:91:13/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:13/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:13/r6.claim: They must leave her watering turn undisturbed, neither preventing her from it nor appropriating it for themselves.
ALUSI:91:13/r6.anchor: فلا تتعرضوا بمنعها عنها في نوبتها ولا تستأثروا بها عليها

ALUSI:91:13/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:13/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:91:13/r7.claim: One view makes the conjunction mean leave God's she-camel together with her watering and do not separate them; al-Alusi calls this far-fetched.
ALUSI:91:13/r7.anchor: وقيل الواو للمعية والمراد ذروا ناقة الله مع سقياها ولا تحولوا بينهما وهو كما ترى

ALUSI:91:13/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:13/r8.speaker: زيد بن علي
ALUSI:91:13/r8.claim: Zayd b. ʿAlī reads Naqat Allah in the nominative, understood as directing their concern to the she-camel and her watering, so they do not slaughter her or monopolize the water.
ALUSI:91:13/r8.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي ناقة الله بالرفع فقيل أي همكم ناقة الله وسقياها

BAGHAWI:91:13/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:13/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:91:13/r1.claim: The Messenger is Salih, who warns the people not to hamstring God's she-camel and not to interfere with its allotted drink from the water.
BAGHAWI:91:13/r1.anchor: { فقال لهم رسول الله } صالح { ناقة الله } أي احذروا عقر ناقة الله .

BAGHAWI:91:13/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:13/r2.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI:91:13/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the accusative naqat Allah implies an omitted command: leave God's she-camel alone.
BAGHAWI:91:13/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج : منصوب على معنى : ذروا ناقة الله ،   { وسقياها } شربها

BAGHAWI:91:13/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:13/r3.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI:91:13/r3.claim: By the same ellipsis, leave her drink alone and do not approach the water on her drinking day.
BAGHAWI:91:13/r3.anchor: أي : ذروا ناقة الله وذروا شربها من الماء ،   فلا تعرضوا للماء يوم شربها

BAYDAWI:91:13/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:91:13/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:91:13/r1.claim: The Messenger tells them to leave God's she-camel alone, beware slaughtering her, and not prevent her from drinking.
BAYDAWI:91:13/r1.anchor: أي ذروا ناقة الله واحذروا عقرها وسقياها وسقيها فلا تذودوها عنها

BIQAI:91:13/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:13/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:13/r1.claim: Saleh warns them because their uprising or denial shows they intend harm to the she-camel.
BIQAI:91:13/r1.anchor: بسبب الانبعاث أو التكذيب الذي دل على قصدهم لها بالأذى

BIQAI:91:13/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:13/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:13/r2.claim: The messenger is named explicitly, and the divine name emphasizes the greatness of their sign and its origin; honoring the messenger and camel honors the one who sent them.
BIQAI:91:13/r2.anchor: الإظهار بالجلالة إشارة إلى عظيم آيتهم وبديع بدايتهم ونهايتهم

BIQAI:91:13/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:13/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:13/r3.claim: He is called a messenger because his role is to convey the message and warn, as he does here.
BIQAI:91:13/r3.anchor: لأن وظيفته الإبلاغ والتحذير الذي ذكر هنا

BIQAI:91:13/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:13/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:13/r4.claim: Repeating God's name in “God's she-camel” increases the warning's gravity: no one who violates what God has claimed as sacred will be spared.

BIQAI:91:13/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:13/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:13/r5.claim: An omitted governing command is understood, such as “leave her” or “beware”; the urgency and impending punishment explain the ellipsis.
BIQAI:91:13/r5.anchor: بحذف العامل إلى ضيق الحال عن ذكره لعظيم الهول

BIQAI:91:13/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:13/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:13/r6.claim: Her watering is the well assigned to her: they must not drive her from it on her turn or harm her; Saleh seems to have repeated the warning after realizing they planned to slaughter her.
BIQAI:91:13/r6.anchor: الماء الذي جعله الله تعالى لها لسقيها وهو بئرها

BIQAI:91:14/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:14/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:14/r9.claim: As an inward allegory, the she-camel is the soul that carries a person through works, a divine gift to preserve and purify rather than corrupt.
BIQAI:91:14/r9.anchor: وكل نفس هي عند صاحبها كالناقة قد أوصى الله صاحبها أن يرعى نعمته

BIQAI:91:14/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:14/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:14/r10.claim: The camel's water signifies remembrance and worship sustaining the soul; neglecting and slaughtering this gift merits destruction.
BIQAI:91:14/r10.anchor: صالح لأن يراد به الذكر والعبادة

IBNASHUR:91:11/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:11/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:11/r5.claim: The object of ‘denied’ is omitted but supplied by the next verse: they denied their Messenger.
IBNASHUR:91:11/r5.anchor: محذوف لدلالة قوله بعده : { فقال لهم رسول الله }

IBNASHUR:91:13/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:13/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:13/r1.claim: The mention of the most wretched man's rising is brought forward because his act is part of their transgression and tied to denial; its placement shows their incitement, while hamstringing still followed the Messenger's warning.
IBNASHUR:91:13/r1.anchor: لأن انبعاث أشقاها لعقر الناقة جزئي من جزئيات طغواهم

IBNASHUR:91:13/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:13/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:13/r3.claim: The fāʾ can coordinate with ‘Thamud denied,’ giving normal sequence: after denying Salih, they received the she-camel sign and warning not to harm it or deny its watering turn.
IBNASHUR:91:13/r3.anchor: عاطفة على { كذبت } فتفيد الترتيب والتعقيب

IBNASHUR:91:13/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:13/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:13/r4.claim: On this sequence, the later denial rejects the threat implicit in the warning; the she-camel sign came after their first rejection, as is usual for prophetic signs and apparent in Hud.
IBNASHUR:91:13/r4.anchor: أي فيما أنذرهم به فعقروها بالتكذيب المذكور أول مرة

IBNASHUR:91:13/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:13/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:13/r5.claim: Alternatively, fāʾ gives only textual sequence, moving from a summary of Thamud's denial to its details; then ‘when their most wretched arose’ need not be treated as fronted from later.
IBNASHUR:91:13/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الفاء للترتيب الذكري المجرد وهي تفيد عطف مفصل على مجمل

IBNASHUR:91:13/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:13/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:13/r6.claim: Plural pronouns return because Thamud is now treated as a people, whereas earlier pronouns followed the tribe's collective name.
IBNASHUR:91:13/r6.anchor: وأعيدت عليهم ضمائر الجمع باعتبار أنهم جمع وإن كانت الضمائر قبله مراعىً فيها أن ثمود اسم قبيلة

IBNASHUR:91:13/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:13/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:13/r7.claim: Nāqata Allāh is accusative as a warning, with an implied ‘beware’; the warning is really against harming the she-camel, expressed by attaching the command to the entity.
IBNASHUR:91:13/r7.anchor: على التحذير ، والتقدير : احذروا ناقة الله

IBNASHUR:91:13/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:13/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:13/r8.claim: The camel is attributed to God because He made it a sign of Salih's truth and its emergence was beyond customary causes.
IBNASHUR:91:13/r8.anchor: وإضافة { ناقة } إلى اسم الجلالة لأنها آية جعلها الله على صدق رسالة صالح

IBNASHUR:91:13/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:13/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:13/r9.claim: Suqyā is a verbal noun of saqā, coordinated with the warning: beware her watering, meaning do not usurp her allotted drink.
IBNASHUR:91:13/r9.anchor: والسقيا : اسم مصدر سَقى ، وهو معطوف على التحذير

IBNASHUR:91:13/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:13/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:13/r10.claim: One construction supplies an omitted noun: ‘beware her watering’ means do not seize her allotted share.

IBNASHUR:91:13/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:13/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:13/r11.claim: Alternatively, the verbal noun names the water itself by using the source for its object; context warns against watering their camels on her allotted day.
IBNASHUR:91:13/r11.anchor: أو أطلق السقيا على الماء الذي تسقى منه إطلاقاً للمصدر على المفعول

IBNASHUR:91:13/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:13/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:13/r12.claim: The context and word suqyā indicate a warning against letting their camels drink from the water on the she-camel's day.
IBNASHUR:91:13/r12.anchor: فإن مادة سقيا تؤذن بأن المراد التحذير من أن يسقوا إبلهم من الماء

IBNASHUR:91:13/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:13/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:13/r13.claim: The implied threat was explicit in the command not to touch the camel with harm, lest painful punishment seize them.
IBNASHUR:91:13/r13.anchor: وهو المصرح به في آية سورة الأعراف ( 73 ) في قوله

IBNATIYYA:91:13/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:13/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:91:13/r1.claim: The accusative “God's she-camel and her drinking turn” depends on an omitted imperative: guard it, leave it alone, or beware of violating its due right.
IBNATIYYA:91:13/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { ناقة الله وسقياها } نصب بفعل مضمر تقديره احفظوا أو ذروا أو احذروا على معنى : احذروا الإخلال بحق ذلك

IBNATIYYA:91:13/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:13/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:91:13/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the she-camel and her allotted drink have already been treated elsewhere in the Qur'an, so he does not repeat that account here.
IBNATIYYA:91:13/r2.anchor: وقد تقدم أمر الناقة والسقيا في غير هذه السورة بما أغنى عن إعادتها

NASAFI:91:13/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:91:13/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:91:13/r1.claim: God's messenger here is Ṣāliḥ, peace be upon him.
NASAFI:91:13/r1.anchor: { فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ الله } صالح عليه السلام

NASAFI:91:13/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:91:13/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:91:13/r2.claim: Ṣāliḥ warns them to protect God's she-camel and its watering; “God's she-camel” is accusative for warning, like “the lion, the lion.”
NASAFI:91:13/r2.anchor: { نَاقَةُ الله } نصب على التحذير أي احذروا عقرها { وسقياها } كقولك : الأسد الأسد

QURTUBI:91:13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:13/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:13/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : " فقال لهم رسول الله " يعني صالحا

QURTUBI:91:13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:13/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:13/r2.claim: ناقة is accusative as a warning formula, like الأسد الأسد or الحذار الحذار.
QURTUBI:91:13/r2.anchor: " ناقة " منصوب على التحذير ، كقولك : الأسد الأسد ، والصبي الصبي ، والحذار الحذار

QURTUBI:91:13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:13/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:13/r3.claim: The warning means they must beware God's she-camel and not hamstring her.
QURTUBI:91:13/r3.anchor: أي احذروا ناقة الله ، أي عقرها

QURTUBI:91:13/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:13/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:91:13/r4.claim: Another interpretation is leave God's she-camel alone, as in 7:73, which says let her graze and do not harm her.
QURTUBI:91:13/r4.anchor: وقيل : ذروا ناقة الله ، كما قال : " هذه ناقة الله لكم آية فذروها تأكل في أرض الله

QURTUBI:91:13/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:13/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:13/r5.claim: The command means to leave the she-camel and her allotted drink alone.

QURTUBI:91:13/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:13/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:13/r6.claim: When they requested a sign, the camel emerged from a rock; she was allotted one day to drink from their well, and they had the next, which burdened them.
QURTUBI:91:13/r6.anchor: فإنهم لما اقترحوا الناقة ، وأخرجها لهم من الصخرة ، جعل لهم شرب يوم من بئرهم ، ولها شرب يوم مكان ذلك ، فشق ذلك عليهم

RAZI:91:13/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:13/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:91:13/r1.claim: The messenger is Ṣāliḥ; when he learned they intended to hamstring the she-camel, he named it as God’s sign of oneness and his prophethood and warned them not to harm it or deny its water.
RAZI:91:13/r1.anchor: المراد من الرسول صالح عليه السلام

RAZI:91:13/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:13/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:91:13/r2.claim: The camel had a drinking day and the people and livestock another; burdened by this, they intended to kill her, while Ṣāliḥ repeatedly warned of punishment, so the brief allusion sufficed.
RAZI:91:13/r2.anchor: وقد بينا في مواضع من هذا الكتاب أنه كان لها شرب يوم

RAZI:91:13/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:13/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:91:13/r3.claim: Nāqata Allāh is an accusative warning construction, like repeating “the lion” or “the child,” with omitted commands to leave her unharmed and protect her watering right.
RAZI:91:13/r3.anchor: ناقة الله } نصب على التحذير ،   كقولك الأسد الأسد
